label: ext.blocktype ext.migration
createStatement: CREATE (b:ext.blocktype {id: $id, name: $name, properties: $properties, requiredProperties: $requiredProperties, semantics: $semantics, status: $status})

createParameters.name: ext.migration

properties.after: the ids of the migrations this one runs after
properties.migrates: the type names whose breaking definition changes this Block covers
properties.rationale: why the breaking definition change is safe or worth its cost
properties.route: the kernelCallback route, relative to the extension's own, that answers the statement transforming existing content; absent for a migration that is rationale alone

createParameters.semantics: The migration Block a breaking type-definition change must travel with. Without a route it is the rationale beside the change, whose content operations are staged in the same group. With a route, a kernelCallback route of its extension, it is executable: the kernel runs it once per instance when it serves a pin, after the migrations of the extensions its extension depends on and those it names in after, and writes the statement the route answers as truth. Validation refuses a breaking ext.blocktype or ext.relationtype change whose group carries no ext.migration covering the type. Never materializes to the working tree. BO_0109_007 BO_0312_001
